## The Geologic Time Scale
<hr>

- **Humans subdivide time into useable units, such as our calendar year, months, weeks, and days** 

<br/>

- **Geologists also subdivide time- breaking it into useable, understandable segments**
    + based on major geologic events
    + based on appearance (and disappearance) of significant life-forms
    + starts with formation of Earth’s crust followed by the appearance of ever-changing forms of life

</div>

## Key Periods of Human History
<hr>
<br/>

<div style="float: left; width: 50%;">

- **We know that humans influence the biosphere - just by being humans**
    + local vs regional vs global

<br/>

- **On geologic times scales humans have existed in the Cenozoic era**
    + our evolutionary trajectory takes us through the Pleistocene and Holocene
    + and at some point a new epoch: *Anthropocene*

<br/>

- **Understanding the pace of human impacts requires knowledge geologic time scales**
    
</div>

<IMG STYLE="position:absolute; TOP:200px; LEFT:550px; WIDTH:550px; HEIGHT:400px" SRC="images/clock.jpg">

## Pleistocene Ice Age (1.8-0.1 mya)
<hr>

<div style="float: left; width: 65%;">

- **Glaciers repeatedly advance from the Arctic over Europe and North America**
    + ice up to a mile thick
    + temperatures ahead of the flow drop significantly.
    
<br/>

- **Animal life evolved (or not) to handle temperature change**
    + new species, range shifts, population declines
    
<br/>

- **Hominid line continues to evolve during the Pleistocene**
    + anatomically modern humans first appear during late stages

<br/>

- **More than 200 genera of very large herbivores go extinct**
    + 95% in North America
    + humans and climate

</div>

<IMG STYLE="position:absolute; TOP:160px; LEFT:700px; WIDTH:360px; HEIGHT:500px" SRC="images/megafauna.png">

## Appalachian Mountains During the Pleistocene 
<hr>
- **Laurentide Ice Sheet covered much of North America but did not extend into the southern Appalachians**

<br/>

<div style="float: right; width: 55%;">

- **Mountains were a major climatic refuge for species displaced by glaciers**
    + preserved ancient lineages of *temperature* plants and animals
    + endemic specie of Appalachia survived this period

<br/>

- **Large mammals (mastodons, mammoths) migrated through Appalachian valleys**

<br/>

- **Post-glacial meltwater created river valleys (e.g., Tennessee and New River basins)**

</div>

<IMG STYLE="position:absolute; TOP:240px; LEFT:30px; WIDTH:450px; HEIGHT:400px" SRC="images/icesheet.jpg">


## Holocene (12,000 -)
<hr>
<br/>

<div style="float: left; width: 50%;">
- **H. sapien the only member of our genus to enter this period**

<br/>

- **Begins after last glacial period, including glacial retreat**
    + Earth experienced a warming trend
    + Perhaps why biodiversity is comparably high
    
<br/>

- **Climate change and megafauna extinction drive massive change in human behaviors**
    
<br/>

- **Rapid proliferation, growth and impacts of the human species worldwide**

</div>

<IMG STYLE="position:absolute; TOP:180px; LEFT:560px; WIDTH:500px; HEIGHT:500px" SRC="images/cartoon.jpg">

## Holocene: Stable/warm climate benefited humans
<hr>

- **Significant advancements in technology and 'urbanization'**
    + resultant increases in human impacts (>local?)

## Neolithic period (12,000-6,000ya)
<hr>
<br/>

<div style="float: left; width: 60%;">

- **Set of developments that appeared in several places independently!**

<br/>

- **Development of agricultural crucial human landmark**
    + plant cultivation and animal domestication
    + irrigation in areas with insufficient rainfall
    + spread from several centers of origin
    
<br/>

- **Origin of agriculture... necessity or opportunity?**

<br/>

- **Whether from migrating farmers or indigenous development, most continents were transformed**

</div>

## Appalachian Mountains During the Holocene/Neolithic 
<hr>

<div style="float: left; width: 53%;">

- **Earliest indigenous peoples arrived as hunter/gathers**
    + relied on foraging, hunting, and fishing
    + shifted to cultivating native crops

<br/>

- **Eastern Agricultural Complex: woodlands of eastern North America was 1 of 10 independent centers of plant domestication**
    + sunflower, goosefoot, squash, and maygrass
    + disappeared after maize was introduced

<br/>

- **Increased sedentism and larger semi-permanent villages along rivers and fertile valleys**
    + regional-scale transition to landscape manipulation and resource intensification.
</div>

## Late Holocene: Review - Industrial Age (1760 -)
<hr>
<br/>
<br/>

<div style="float: left; width: 50%;">

- **Economic and social organization that began around 1760 in Great Britain** 
    + factory's of production (trade, farming, natural resources) allowed it to happen
    
<br/>

- **Replacement of hand tools with power-driven machines**
    + power loom, steam engine, iron making

<br/>

- **Appalachian Context: The region became a center for coal mining, fueling industrial growth at the cost of environmental health.**
 
 </div>
 
<IMG STYLE="position:absolute; TOP:240px; LEFT:560px; WIDTH:500px; HEIGHT:400px" SRC="images/coal.png">


## Late Holocene: Review - Industrial Age (1760 -)
<hr>
<br/>
<br/>

<div style="float: left; width: 45%;">

- **Every aspect of daily life was influenced in some way**

<br/>

- **Average income and population began to exhibit unprecedented sustained growth**
    + creation of middle class
    
<br/>

- **Represents the starting point for serious atmospheric change**
    + based on fossil fuel emissions
    + https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=kCmwKbVFbWg (bar chart race)
    
 </div>
 
<IMG STYLE="position:absolute; TOP:220px; LEFT:530px; WIDTH:600px; HEIGHT:400px" SRC="images/airpoll.jpg">

## NOW: The Great Acceleration
<hr>

- **Period of rapid socio-economic and environmental following World War II (>1950)**
    + Coincided with the Atomic Age and the Cold War tech race
    + non-official start of the Anthropocene

<br/>

- **Key drivers: Population boom, industrial expansion, globalization, rise of consumer economies**
    + global population has tripled in just 75 years
    
<br/>

- **Introduction of synthetic chemicals, plastics, fertilizers, and global supply chains**

<br/>

- **Technological growth: Cars, highways, electronics, suburban sprawl**

<br/>

- **Appalachian context: Infrastructure expansion, coal demand spikes, and federal investments for energy**

## Key Periods of Human History: The Anthropocene Epoch
<hr>
<div style="float: left; width: 50%;">

- **New geologic era?**
    + proposal submitted
    + would mark end of the Holocene
    
<br/>

- **Many geologist criticize the idea**
    + hard to define a period when you are in it
    
</div>

<div style="float: right; width: 50%;">
- **Interval of time where humans dominate key processes on Earth**
    + anthropo, for “man,” and cene, for “new”


 </div>

## The Great Acceleration: Post 1950
<hr>
<br/>

<div style="float: left; width: 55%;">

- **Dramatic, continuous surge in growth rate across a large range of measures of human activity**

<br/>

- **Socioeconomic parameters:  population, economics, water usage, food production, transportation, technology**

<br/>

- **Earth system parameters: green house gases, surface temperature, and natural resource usage**

<br/>

- **Post-war revival age**
    + fossil energy and new technology flooding the markets

 </div>
 
<IMG STYLE="position:absolute; TOP:180px; LEFT:600px; WIDTH:550px; HEIGHT:450px" SRC="images/box.png">

## Appalachia in the Anthropocene: Enviromental
<hr>
<br/>

<div style="float: left; width: 48%;">

- **Remains a major U.S. coal producer**
    + mountaintop removal flattened 500+ peaks
    + now includes fracking (oil/natural gas) in Marcellus shale

<br/>

- **Continued land transformation**
    + clear-cutting removed old-growth forests
    + erosion, stream pollution from mining/logging

<br/>

- **Climate Trends include warmer winters, heavier spring rainfall**

 </div>
    
<IMG STYLE="position:absolute; TOP:200px; LEFT:525px; WIDTH:500px; HEIGHT:450px" SRC="images/mining.jpg">

## Appalachia in the Anthropocene: Soceital
<hr>
<br/>

<div style="float: left; width: 55%;">

- **Boom-Bust Economy: Jobs rose with coal, fell with automation/global shift**
    + Persistent poverty, youth outmigration

<br/>

- **Health & Justice: Higher rates of cancer, respiratory illness near mining sites**
    + Poor & rural communities hit hardest

<br/>

- **Resistance Movements: Groups like Appalachian Voices fight for justice**

<br/>

- **Cultural Resilience:Local stewardship rooted in lived experience**
    + Strong land ties, storytelling, music traditions
    
 </div>
    
<IMG STYLE="position:absolute; TOP:200px; LEFT:600px; WIDTH:450px; HEIGHT:450px" SRC="images/stopremoval.jpg">
